claims.explanation: SC-9 is a PKC activator, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence on PKC signaling pathways that are altered by specific mutations. Sensitizing features include activation of RAS/MAPK (NF1, RB1 loss) and PI3K/AKT (PTEN loss) pathways that may create synthetic lethality with PKC activation, as well as SWI/SNF complex defects (SMARCA4, SMARCB1) and EWSR1-FLI1 fusion. Protective features include constitutive PI3K/AKT activation via PIK3CA mutation and chromatin modifier mutations (KMT2D, ARID1A, EP300) that may blunt PKC-induced differentiation/apoptosis.

RAS/MAPK activation may create dependency on PKC signaling

chromatin remodeling defect may impair PKC-induced differentiation/apoptosis
SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling defect may protect from PKC-induced death
histone acetyltransferase loss may blunt PKC-induced transcriptional changes
RB1 loss impairs cell cycle checkpoint, enhancing apoptosis

SMARCB1 deficiency (rhabdoid tumor) may sensitize to PKC activation
Wnt/beta-catenin activation may protect from PKC-mediated death
